title: Delta-driven Eval Harness and Dynamic Threshold Synthesizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an evaluation harness and an automated threshold synthesizer that measures per-profile quality deltas (float32 -> int8/int4; AWQ/GPTQ variants) and produces conservative, explainable gate thresholds for rollout. The harness emphasizes delta metrics that are sensitive to real user tasks: structured extraction fidelity, ranking stability, token-level perplexity shifts on long prefixes, and downstream regression impact on eval suites. The Dynamic Threshold Synthesizer (DTS) will use these deltas plus cost/latency profiles to recommend profile-specific gate values and an ordered fallback policy (e.g., int4 -> int8 -> float32) with per-route confidence bands.
acceptance_criteria: DTS outputs a recommended threshold (0-1 scale) for any given model+quant-profile with an explanation string
Eval harness computes delta metrics across a rubric of 12 task-specific datasets and stores summary CSVs
Automated canary flow: when a profile is deployed to 10% traffic, the system flags if observed deltas exceed recommended thresholds and triggers rollback hooks
Documentation + runbook: engineers can run offline calibration sweeps and reproduce DTS recommendations
Benchmarks: DTS recommendations reduce customer-visible regressions by at least 60% vs naive fixed thresholds in our simulated workloads
approach: 1) Instrument a delta-centric eval pipeline: ingest golden outputs and baseline float outputs, then run target quantized profile and compute asymmetric deltas (precision-weighted F1, semantic drift, and rank-stability). 2) Implement a lightweight meta-model (Bayesian optimizer with monotonic prior) that synthesizes a threshold maximizing a utility function balancing quality delta, latency reduction, and cost savings. 3) Produce human-readable rationales and a recommended rollback/fallback order. 4) Integrate with console rollouts: expose recommended gates and a metric window for live rejection/rollback.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Overfitting DTS to our eval set: mitigate with cross-task holdouts and randomized prompt augmentation. - False negatives: thresholds too lax may allow regressions through; DTS will bias conservative by default and provide explainable error bars. - Operational complexity: adding per-profile thresholds increases surface area; we'll centralize recommendations in a single service and surface only approved thresholds in Console.
milestones: M2: DTS prototype + Bayesian optimizer integration (2025-03-14)
M3: Canary integration with rollouts + runbook (2025-03-28)
updates: 2025-02-20: Initial spike completed. Prototype harness runs AWQ/GPTQ variants against three toy tasks. Observed asymmetric degradation patterns on extraction tasks.
2025-02-26: Design review with PM and Design. Decided to prioritize per-route thresholds where downstream task loss is asymmetric (e.g., extraction > generation).
2025-03-03: Bayesian optimizer integrated into prototype. Early runs produce conservative thresholds that match manual tuning on two models.
2025-03-07: Engineering review: added monotonic prior to optimizer to prefer higher fidelity at lower threshold values. Added schema for explanation strings returned by DTS.
2025-03-11: Began wiring canary hooks into Console feature-flag service. Need security sign-off for synthetic traffic generation (ticket raised to SecOps).
next_steps: 1) Finish integration tests for canary rollback logic. 2) Run a 10-model sweep (mix of open and curated models) and export CSVs for PM review. 3) Add per-route metadata tags in Console to accept or override DTS recommendations.
notes: This ticket focuses on the calibration and recommendation layer, not on changing the runtime quant kernels. Coordinate with runtime and infra teams for rollout orchestration. When DTS is mature, we will propose an experimental default for Dedicated customers with opt-in toggles.
